source.title: Characterizing Learning Curves During Language Model Pre-Training: Learning, Forgetting, and Stability
source.authors: Tyler A. Chang; Zhuo-Wen Tu; Benjamin K. Bergen

record.tranche_reason: The study reports aggregate pre-training loss curves relevant to the loss-bump component of V2, but does not measure induction heads or in-context learning.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Olsson et al.'s induction-head result as related work; it does not measure induction heads or token-index in-context learning. The only directly named outcome relevant to a claim version is its description of aggregate corpus-level loss as smoothly decreasing, without a bump.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Olsson et al. (2022) only as related work. It never identifies induction or previous-token heads, never measures in-context learning (loss against token index), and never looks for a phase change. Its remark that corpus-level loss decreases smoothly is a passing qualitative description, not an analysis of the loss bump. The plot uses log-scaled steps with 128-token sequences, so it cannot show whether a bump co-occurs with induction-head formation. The record's T2/'tests' and its V2 'challenges' label are not justified.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that sudden per-example loss changes that are consistent across seeds imply sequential dependencies between capabilities. They characterize learning as early n-gram learning followed by gradual refinement of tail n-gram predictions. Frequent tokens, n-gram-probable tokens and frequent contexts are learned earlier and more stably.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes aggregate and individual-token surprisal curves during GPT-2-architecture pre-training; it does not use the original induction-head identification or in-context-learning measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual token-in-context loss curves show sudden drops and increases that recur across five seeds and data shuffles, despite i.i.d. data. Model surprisals peak in correlation with 1- to 5-gram models in order (Fig. 2, Fig. 3, §5.2, §7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-model pre-training contains sequential, seed-robust learning dependencies (n-gram stages, then refinement), visible in per-example rather than aggregate loss.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Induction heads and in-context learning are not measured, so the loss-curve result cannot establish their presence, absence, or timing. The paper describes the relevant aggregate curve qualitatively rather than reporting a numeric bump measure.
record.rows_left_out: No other findings were extracted: individual-token loss fluctuations, n-gram correlations, and learning-curve metrics do not measure induction-head behaviour or the token-index in-context-learning gain specified in the claim.

untested.parts: All: no induction-head formation timing, no ICL score, no analysis of a loss bump.
All: the data and training setup are not varied with respect to induction heads or ICL.
All: the reported sequential n-gram stages are not induction-head sub-steps.

record.verdict_notes: Five 124M GPT-2-architecture runs trained on OSCAR English with 128-token sequences. Induction heads appear only in the related-work citation. No verdicts are warranted; the record's V2 'challenges' label should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: Induction-head formation, composition with a previous-token head, and the [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
The study does not measure induction-head formation, in-context-learning gains, or their timing relative to each other; it reports only aggregate loss curves.
Whether induction heads account for most in-context learning in large transformers.
Induction behaviour across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Whether data or training setup changes induction-head formation or the persistence of in-context learning.
Mechanisms carrying few-shot task learning versus repeated-token copying.
Whether induction-head formation consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: five autoregressive Transformer language-model pre-training runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Reported aggregate corpus-level loss (mean surprisal) curves during pre-training.
rows.measure: Aggregate corpus-level loss curve; whether it exhibits a bump.
rows.value: Corpus-level loss is described as smoothly decreasing; the five loss curves are described as nearly identical.
rows.note: This bears on the loss-bump component of V2 only. The paper does not report a numeric bump measure or assess induction heads or in-context learning.
rows.check: The aggregate loss curve (Fig. 4) is described only as 'nearly identical across runs'. 'Smoothly decreasing corpus-level loss' appears as an aside in the introduction. The study does not examine the curve for the small induction-head bump and has no induction-head or ICL measure to time it against. It cannot bear on V2. Footnote 4 mentions a small temporary loss increase in one run near step 10^5.7, which is an instability in that run, not the phase-change bump. The row should be dropped or set to versions ['none'].

source_check.locator_found: §1: smoothly decreasing corpus-level loss; §3.1: five 124M-parameter GPT-2-architecture runs trained for 1M steps; Appendix A.1, Figure 4: mean-surprisal curves nearly identical across runs.
